facts.claim: No late fee or penalty fee of any kind may be charged to an account in a registered non-profit segment. A reduced late fee for charities was proposed and rejected because NP-7 allows no fee at all.
facts.current_scope: From episode 3, late fees on invoices due before day 1000, and every penalty fee (including the returned-payment fee), for every registered non-profit segment.

facts.claim: Every fee is an integer number of cents. A percentage fee is rounded half up to the cent, never with banker's rounding.
An invoice is late when today is more than 14 days after its due day; the late fee is 5% of the amount, at least 100 cents; otherwise 0.

The foundation segment, displayed as "Registered foundation", is for registered non-profit foundations; the cooperative segment, displayed as "Member cooperative", is for member-owned for-profit cooperatives. Statement lines show a segment's display name instead of its code.

Regulation NP-9 replaces NP-7 for late fees on invoices due on or after day 1000: a late invoice of any registered non-profit account due on or after day 1000 has a flat 200-cent late fee. Earlier invoices and all penalty fees stay under NP-7.
FeePolicy.returned_payment_fee(account, amount_cents) charges a bounced payment 2.5% of amount_cents, but at least 250 cents.
The association segment, displayed as "Registered association", is for registered non-profit associations.
fee_forecast returns the late fee for each given day, in order.
FeePolicy.collection_penalty(account, invoice, today) charges 15% of amount_cents, but at least 500 cents, once today is more than 60 days after invoice.due_day; otherwise 0.
A late fee is computed from the invoice and the day it is requested; it is never stored on the invoice, so a statement always shows the fee as of its statement day.
FeePolicy methods depend only on their arguments and module constants; they keep no caches or counters, so any fee can be recomputed for any day.
Fee calculations are methods on FeePolicy rather than helpers spread across statements and invoices, so a fee rule changes in one place.
Day counts, percentages and minimum amounts used by fee rules are named constants at the top of fees.py, so every fee parameter can be reviewed in one place.
A late fee is a charge for paying late rather than a sale, so no sales tax is added to it on invoices or statements.
Finance reconciles fee income separately from invoice revenue, so the monthly revenue export reports each kind of fee in its own column.
When support upholds a customer's dispute of a late fee, the fee is reversed with a credit note; neither the invoice nor the fee rule is edited.
A statement once showed a late fee one day before it was due because the day count was off by one; boundary days now get their own visible test.
Each overdue invoice carries its own late fee; late fees are never combined or averaged across an account's invoices.
The platform bills in a single currency; a late fee is expressed in the same cents as the invoice it applies to.
Any change to a fee amount or fee rule is reviewed by finance before release, because fees appear on customer statements; a code-only review was considered and rejected.
Customer-facing text that mentions a late fee states the invoice ID, the due day and the fee in cents, without legal abbreviations.
Due days, statement days and today are integer day numbers counted from the billing epoch, so comparing two days is plain integer arithmetic.
An invoice holds its amount in amount_cents; conversion to currency units for display happens only when a statement is printed.
The due day is set when an invoice is issued and never moves; a payment plan issues new invoices instead of changing due days.
Each invoice ID identifies exactly one invoice for its whole life, so statements, payments and credit notes refer to invoices by ID.
Once issued, an invoice's amount, due day and account never change.
A wrong invoice is corrected with a credit note and a replacement invoice rather than by editing it, so billing history stays auditable; editing in place was rejected.
Calendar dates were considered for billing arithmetic and rejected because month lengths and time zones made due-day comparisons error-prone.
An account's segment code must be a key of the segment table in accounts.py; an unknown code is rejected when the account is created.
Account IDs carry no meaning; code never parses them for region, size or segment.
Once a segment code is used it is never renamed, because stored accounts and exports refer to it; only its display name may change.
Segments are defined in a single table mapping each code to its display name in accounts.py, so adding a segment is a one-line change; a class per segment was rejected.
Closing an account never deletes its invoices; any outstanding invoice stays collectible.
Each statement line shows the invoice ID, the account's segment and the late fee as of the statement day.
A statement is produced for one statement day, and every fee on it is computed as of that day.
Lines appear with the oldest due day first, so the most overdue invoices lead the statement.
An account with more than twenty open invoices receives one consolidated statement per month instead of one per invoice.
Under regulation CP-3, every statement that shows a late fee also shows the due day of the invoice it applies to, so the customer can see why the fee applies.
An unallocated payment is applied to the account's invoice with the earliest due day before any other invoice.
A partial payment is recorded against its invoice but never changes the invoice's amount or due day.
Customers receive one payment reminder the day after an invoice's due day.
Regulation DS-2 requires every payment record to be kept for seven years after the invoice it settles.
Regulation PC-1 forbids adding a surcharge to an invoice because the customer pays it by card.
Charging daily interest on overdue invoices was considered and rejected in favour of a single late fee per invoice, which customers found easier to understand.
Billing code depends only on the Python standard library, so it runs wherever the platform's Python runs.
Existing public billing classes, methods and functions keep their names and parameters; new behaviour is added with new methods.
Each billing rule is covered by a test under tests/ that runs with python3 -m unittest discover.
Billing code runs in one thread with no network access; no locking or retries are needed.
Tests pass today as an explicit day number instead of reading a clock, so every fee test is deterministic; freezing the system clock was rejected.
The reason behind each billing rule is kept as project knowledge, so maintainers can find why a rule exists before changing it.
A fee test that read the system clock failed on the last day of a month; the fix was to pass day numbers explicitly.

forbidden_claims.claim: Only the charity segment is exempt from late fees.
Registered non-profits never pay a late fee, whatever the due day.
NP-9 also replaces NP-7 for penalty fees such as the returned-payment fee.
NP-9 applies regardless of the invoice due day.
NP-9's flat fee applies to the collection penalty.
Non-profits pay a reduced percentage fee.
Percentage fees may use banker's rounding.
